title: Introducing NVFP4 for Efficient and Accurate Low-Precision Inference
authors: Eduardo Alvarez, et al. (NVIDIA)

findings.claim: NVFP4 costs 4.5 bits per value including its per-16 FP8 scale.

quantities.condition: NVFP4 format cost per element incl. block scale

findings.bears_on: The effective width of '4-bit' activations is 4.5 bits, not 4, so the FP4 floor should use 4.5.
findings.audit: 2026-10-17 sample audit: quote yes, claim yes, quantities yes

findings.claim: PTQ of DeepSeek-R1-0528 (671B) to NVFP4 weights and activations loses at most 1% accuracy versus FP8.

findings.bears_on: Production-scale evidence that 4.5-bit matmul inputs retain quality in inference; residual and attention paths not covered.

authors: Saleh Ashkboos, Amirkeivan Mohtashami, Maximilian L. Croci, Bo Li, Pashmina Cameron, Martin Jaggi, et al.

findings.claim: Hadamard rotations remove outliers so weights, matmul-input activations and KV cache all run at 4 bits; Llama-2-70B loses 0.47 perplexity.

quantities.condition: Llama-2-70B W4A4KV4 PTQ, per-token scale; WikiText-2 ppl 3.32 -> 3.79 (Table 1); inference only
Llama-2-70B, asymmetric group-128 KV quantization, same run

findings.bears_on: Supports a central b_a of about 4 bits for matmul inputs in inference.

findings.claim: QuaRot keeps the residual stream itself in 16-bit; quantizing the residual is listed as future work.
findings.quote: Opportunities to build on QuaRot include quantizing the residuals and extending the method to mixture-of-experts architectures.
findings.bears_on: The 4-bit result does not cover the residual vector that crosses a pipeline boundary, so b_a=4 for that vector is an extrapolation.

findings.claim: Llama-3 models degrade much more: Llama-3-70B perplexity rises from 2.86 to 6.66 at W4A4 (5.51 with group-128).
findings.quote: is more sensitive to quantization as we can see a higher gap between the quantized and FP16 models

quantities.condition: Llama-3-70B W4A4KV4: WikiText-2 ppl 2.86 -> 6.66 (QuaRot), 5.51 (QuaRot-128G); large loss

findings.bears_on: Models trained on more tokens are harder to quantize, pushing b_a above 4 for retained quality in newer models.

findings.claim: With everything else in full precision, a 3-bit KV cache costs at most 0.21 perplexity (0.07 on Llama-2-70B).
findings.quote: The results show a negligible (at most 0.21) perplexity degradation up to 3-bit KV cache (0.07 for Llama 2-70B model).

quantities.condition: Llama-2-70B, group-128 asymmetric, +0.07 ppl; inference

findings.bears_on: Places retained-quality KV at about 3 bits with simple quantization.

title: Does compressing activations help model parallel training?
authors: Song Bian, Dacheng Li, Hongyi Wang, Eric P. Xing, Shivaram Venkataraman

findings.claim: In BERT-Large, singular values show gradients are low-rank but activations are not.
findings.quote: The result shows that the gradient is low-rank but the activation is not.
findings.bears_on: Argues against a small linear d_eff for unmodified activations; supports intrinsic_dim near 1.

findings.claim: Learned autoencoders compressing the 1024-dim activation to 50 or 100 dims (about 10-20x) are the only method that both speeds up training and keeps accuracy.
findings.quote: Takeaway 5 Among all evaluated methods, AE is the best strategy to compress activation over pre-training. It achieves higher pre-training throughput and preserves the model’s accuracy.

quantities.condition: AE encoder dim 100 of hidden 1024 (and 50 = ~20x); BERT-Large 345M; last 12 layers; fine-tuning loss within ~3% except CoLA/RTE
derived: AE dim 50 / hidden 1024

findings.bears_on: A learned bottleneck trained with the model reaches ~10-20x at small scale, a precedent for small d_eff.

findings.claim: Quantization and Top-K hurt accuracy when compressing activations during pre-training.
findings.quote: In conclusion, it is not a good choice to compress the activation by using quantization or Top-K.
findings.bears_on: At 345M, direct 2-8 bit quantization of boundary activations was not lossless in pre-training; tempers low b_a.

findings.claim: Compression ratios tested matched the autoencoders.
findings.quote: we compress the activation around 10 and 20 times.
findings.bears_on: Gives the comparison scale for the 10-20x autoencoder result.

findings.claim: In tensor parallelism, the learned linear encoder is applied before the all-reduce, so the partial sums themselves are summed in the compressed space.
findings.quote: For AE, we compress the activation before the all-reduce step and invoke the all-reduce function as usual.
findings.bears_on: A linear projection commutes with the sum, so a learned bottleneck compresses TP partial sums at the AE's 10-20x without a high-precision reduction step.

findings.claim: Compressing the activations of the first layers harms accuracy much more than compressing the last layers.
findings.quote: Compressing the activation for the initial layers harms the accuracy of the model.
findings.bears_on: b_a is not uniform across depth: early-layer boundaries need more bits, so one b_a for every boundary is an average.

title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
authors: Tim Dettmers, Mike Lewis, Younes Belkada, Luke Zettlemoyer

findings.claim: Int8 activations with a 16-bit side path for a few outlier feature dimensions give degradation-free inference up to 175B parameters.

quantities.condition: OPT-175B/BLOOM inference; matmul inputs; outlier dims kept in 16-bit; no degradation

findings.bears_on: Sets 8 bits as a safe, lossless activation width in inference; an upper anchor for b_a.

findings.claim: Fewer than 0.1% of activation values need 16 bits; the rest are 8-bit.
findings.quote: we also include a new mixed-precision decomposition scheme, which isolates the outlier feature dimensions into a 16-bit matrix multiplication while still more than 99.9% of values are multiplied in 8-bit

quantities.condition: fraction of activation values kept in 16-bit (outlier feature dims)

findings.bears_on: Outliers are sparse and systematic, so their bit cost is small once located; slightly raises effective b_a above 8 only marginally.

findings.claim: Large-magnitude outlier features emerge in all layers from about 6.7B parameters and break naive low-bit activation quantization.
findings.quote: the sparse but systematic large magnitude outlier features that ruin quantization precision once they emerge in all transformer layers starting at scales of 6.7B parameters

title: MegaScale-MoE: Large-Scale Communication-Efficient Training of Mixture-of-Experts Models in Production
authors: Chao Jin, Ziheng Jiang, Zhihao Bai, Zheng Zhong, Juncai Liu, Xiang Li, Ningxin Zheng, Xi Wang, et al.

findings.claim: In production FP8 MoE training the forward TP reduce-scatter of partial sums becomes an FP8 all-to-all with FP32 reduction; plain precision reduction misaligned the loss, which per-token (forward) and per-channel, 128-grouped (backward) scales fixed.
findings.quote: Similar to DP reduce-scatter compression, we replace BF16 TP reduce-scatter with FP8 all-to-all in forward propagation and perform reduction in FP32 precision. In the corresponding backward propagation, we apply FP8 all-gather for gradients. Notably, simply reducing precision leads to loss misalignment with BF16 training. To mitigate this, we apply per-token activation quantization for forward communication and per-channel quantization for backward communication.

quantities.condition: forward TP partial sums E4M3 with a per-token scale, sent by all-to-all and summed in FP32; backward activation-gradients E4M3 per-channel in 128-token groups; FP8 and BF16 loss consistent for a 35B MoE from scratch and a 176B MoE continued (Figure 19); gap and tokens not reported

findings.bears_on: 8-bit TP partial sums work at production scale only when the sum is taken in high precision after transport; a naive low-precision reduction does not.

findings.claim: A production-oriented serving stack chooses 8-bit activations with 4-bit weights and 4-bit KV.
findings.quote: we introduce QoQ, a W4A8KV4 quantization algorithm with 4-bit weight, 8-bit activation, and 4-bit KV cache.

quantities.condition: W4A8KV4 serving, Llama-3-8B to Qwen1.5-72B; inference
same; SmoothAttention to limit KV4 loss

findings.bears_on: Shows practitioners still keep activations at 8 bits when accuracy matters; supports the high end of b_a.

title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache
authors: Zirui Liu, Jiayi Yuan, Hongye Jin, Shaochen Zhong, Zhaozhuo Xu, Vladimir Braverman, et al.

findings.claim: Per-channel keys and per-token values at 2 bits keep almost the same quality on Llama, Falcon and Mistral.
findings.quote: From this analysis, we developed a tuning-free 2bit KV cache quantization algorithm named KIVI. With hardware-friendly implementation, KIVI can enable Llama, Falcon, and Mistral models to maintain almost the same quality

quantities.condition: group size 32 plus up to 128 most recent tokens kept full precision; 7B-13B models; inference

findings.bears_on: Sets the central retained-quality KV width at about 2 bits.

findings.claim: The most recent tokens' KV are kept in full precision.
findings.quote: the residual key cache and value cache are kept in full precision
findings.bears_on: Effective KV width is slightly above 2 bits for short contexts.

title: SpinQuant: LLM Quantization with Learned Rotations
authors: Zechun Liu, Changsheng Zhao, Igor Fedorov, Bilge Soran, Dhruv Choudhary, Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi, et al.

findings.claim: Learned rotations bring W4A4KV4 within 1.7 zero-shot points of full precision on LLaMA-2-70B.
findings.quote: In 4-4-4 quantized LLaMA-2 7B/13B/70B models, SpinQuant had leaves only a 2.9/1.4/1.7 accuracy gap to the corresponding full-precision network

quantities.condition: LLaMA-2-70B W4A4KV4 PTQ with learned rotations; -1.7 points avg zero-shot; inference only
same configuration

findings.bears_on: Strengthens 4 bits as the central inference value for matmul-input activations.

findings.claim: Llama-3-8B is harder to quantize; learned rotations close up to 45.1% of QuaRot's remaining gap.
findings.quote: In particular, for LLaMA-3 8B models that are hard to quantize, SpinQuant reduces the gap to full precision by up to 45.1% relative to QuaRot.
findings.bears_on: Retained quality at 4 bits needs increasingly elaborate transforms for heavily trained models.

title: CoLA: Compute-Efficient Pre-Training of LLMs via Low-Rank Activation
authors: Ziyue Liu, Ruijie Zhang, Zhengyang Wang, Mingsong Yan, Zi Yang, Paul Hovland et al.

findings.claim: CoLA's low-rank bottleneck layers halve computing cost without hurting performance (60M-7B).
findings.quote: The default rank choices reduce half the computing cost, without harming the model performance.

quantities.condition: CoLA vs full-rank, compute to equal perplexity

findings.bears_on: m_A about 2 on GaLore-style short budgets; low-rank activations also narrow internal boundaries.

title: TACO: Efficient Communication Compression of Intermediate Tensors for Scalable Tensor-Parallel LLM Training
authors: Man Liu, Xingchen Liu, Xingjian Tian, Bing Lu, Shengkay Lyu, Shengquan Yin, Wenjing Huang, Zheng Wei, Hairui Zhao, Guangming Tan, Dingwen Tao

findings.claim: FP8 compression of tensor-parallel intermediate tensors, after a per-block RMS rescale and Hadamard rotation with two scales per 256-entry block, costs +0.70% validation loss on GPT-6.7B and +0.03% on Qwen2.5-7B.
findings.quote: For GPT 6.7B, TACO achieves a final validation loss of 2.570587, compared to 2.552718 for baseline, corresponding to a marginal degradation of +0.70%. Similarly, on Qwen-2.5 7B, TACO reaches a loss of 2.257332 versus 2.256751 for the baseline, resulting in an extremely small degradation of +0.03%.

quantities.condition: derived: FP8 E4M3 + 2 scalars per 256-entry block, assumed FP32 (8 + 64/256); TP intermediate tensors (activations forward, activation-gradients backward), TP4; GPT-6.7B on the Pile +0.70%, Qwen2.5-7B +0.03%; 10,000-iteration runs, tokens not stated

findings.bears_on: TP boundary tensors at about 8.25 bits cost under 1% at 7B, but only after conditioning; short runs.

findings.claim: Standard per-tensor FP8 on TP intermediate tensors diverges (validation loss 5.61 vs 2.39 BF16), INT8 after the transform diverges, E5M2 costs 24.1%, and TAH-Quant costs 2.88%.
findings.quote: The empirical evidence reveals that naively applying standard NVFP8 compression to TP intermediate tensors leads to immediate and catastrophic divergence, with the validation loss spiking to 5.605692.

quantities.condition: per-tensor FP8 on TP intermediate tensors, GPT-350M TP4, 10,000 iterations: val loss 5.61 vs BF16 2.39; ASH+INT8 reaches 68.1; ASH+E5M2 3.31 (+24.1%); TAH-Quant +2.88%

findings.bears_on: Negative results: 8 bits per TP entry is not automatically safe; the format and conditioning decide it.

title: FP8 Formats for Deep Learning
authors: Paulius Micikevicius, Dusan Stosic, Neil Burgess, Marius Cornea, Pradeep Dubey, Richard Grisenthwaite et al.

findings.claim: FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) training matches 16-bit result quality on models up to 175B with unchanged hyperparameters.
findings.quote: We demonstrate the efficacy of the FP8 format on a variety of image and language tasks, effectively matching the result quality achieved by 16-bit training sessions.
findings.bears_on: 8-bit activations and weights in matmuls at m_A about 1 per FLOP.

title: Nemotron-H: A Family of Accurate and Efficient Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Models
authors: NVIDIA (Aaron Blakeman, Aarti Basant, Abhinav Khattar, Adithya Renduchintala, et al.)

findings.claim: Nemotron-H-56B was pretrained on 20T tokens with FP8 per-tensor current scaling in the forward and backward passes of the linear layers: E4M3 for weights and activations, E5M2 for gradients, with the first and last 4 layers in BF16.
findings.quote: We quantized both the forward and backward passes of the linear layers. As in Micikevicius et al. (2022), we use a hybrid FP8 approach which uses E4M3 for weight and activation tensors, and E5M2 for the gradient tensors.

quantities.condition: forward activations E4M3, one FP32 scale per tensor (negligible); first 4 and last 4 layers BF16; Nemotron-H-56B / 20T tokens; typical relative loss gap <0.1% vs BF16 (finding /2)
backward activation-gradients E5M2, per-tensor scale; same run

findings.bears_on: The largest published low-precision pretraining: 8 bits per activation and activation-gradient entry with a per-tensor scale, at 56B parameters and 20T tokens.

findings.claim: FP8 loss runs above BF16 by typically under 0.1%, but the gap widens in the last quarter of training; downstream scores were equal or better.
findings.quote: We observed that the log-likelihood loss curves for FP8 pre-training experiments were almost always higher than for their BF16 counterparts, but by a surprisingly small amount, with typical relative gaps less than 0.1% on both training and validation. This loss gap tended to decrease as training progressed but then widened in the last quarter of training.

quantities.condition: upper value of the typical gap; Figure 5 pair: 8B Transformer, 3T tokens, BF16 vs FP8

findings.bears_on: The 8-bit penalty is about 0.1% and not monotone in tokens; the authors add that FP8 recipes had to be validated on at least 8B parameters because smaller-model results did not generalize (Section 2.3).

title: Heterogeneous Low-Bandwidth Pre-Training of LLMs
authors: Yazan Obeidi, Amir Sarfi, Joel Lidin, Paul Janson, Eugene Belilovsky

findings.claim: Subspace compression of pipeline activations and activation-gradients at 87.5% (8x), combined with SparseLoCo data parallelism, costs 5.9% loss at 1B on 10B tokens.
findings.quote: Table 6 confirms that PP-compression remains effective at the 1B scale, with 87.5% compression yielding a loss of 2.910 compared to the baseline 2.747—a degradation consistent with smaller model scales.

quantities.condition: derived: 16 bits x (1 - 0.875); SSN-style orthonormal subspace in both directions; 1B, DCLM, sequence 1024, 10B tokens with SparseLoCo; loss 2.910 vs 2.747 (derived +5.9%)

findings.bears_on: An independent 8x pipeline-boundary point at 1B with a larger penalty (about 6%).

title: Protocol Models: Scaling Decentralized Training with Communication-Efficient Model Parallelism
authors: Sameera Ramasinghe, Thalaiyasingam Ajanthan, Gil Avraham, Yan Zuo, Alexander Long

findings.claim: Constraining weights so that inter-stage activations and their gradients lie in a shared subspace allows 99% compression of pipeline-parallel traffic with no convergence loss.
findings.quote: enabling up to 99% compression with no convergence degradation with negligible memory/compute overhead

quantities.condition: activations and activation-gradients between pipeline stages; 8B LLaMA; 64 L4 GPUs over 60-350 Mbps

findings.bears_on: Lowers b_a at a model-parallel boundary by ~100x when the architecture is trained to be subspace-constrained, the case NCI's sharding bound charges.

findings.claim: The subspace has rank 40, which gives the 100x.
findings.quote: We initialize Uk with isotropic Gaussian noise and set k = 40, achieving 100× compression.

quantities.condition: chosen subspace rank sufficient for convergence (a design choice, not a measured intrinsic dimension)

findings.bears_on: Suggests an effective d of order 10^1-10^2 per boundary token in trained-for-compression models.

findings.claim: Generic compressors (top-k, SVD, quantization) fail to converge at 100x on the same boundary traffic.
findings.quote: Top-k, low-rank (SVD), and quantization fail to converge at 100× compression
findings.bears_on: Off-the-shelf activation compression is much weaker; the 100x needs architecture changes.

findings.claim: Without compression the decentralized run was 13x slower than the centralized one.
findings.quote: the decentralized setting w/o compression was 13x slower.

quantities.condition: decentralized, uncompressed, vs centralized

findings.bears_on: Model-parallel boundaries are the bottleneck once workers do not hold a full model.

findings.claim: Pluralis constrains projection weights to a shared low-dimensional subspace so activations and activation gradients crossing pipeline stages compress by up to 99% with no convergence loss.
findings.quote: We propose a novel compression algorithm that compresses both forward and backward passes, enabling up to 99% compression with no convergence degradation with negligible memory/compute overhead.

quantities.condition: forward activations and backward gradients; architecture-constrained; up to 8B, 80 Mbps links
derived: 99% compression -> subspace k ~ d/100 (plus token ids for the embedding term)

findings.bears_on: The strongest attack on NCI: a model designed to be split cuts boundary bits ~100x, lowering the sharding floor ~100x.

findings.claim: An 8B LLaMA split across four regions over the internet converged on par with datacenter baselines.
findings.quote: Further, we successfully train an 8B-parameter LLaMA model (Dubey et al., 2024) with layers split across four different geographical regions, connected via the internet, and achieve convergence on par with baselines utilizing datacenter-grade connections.
findings.bears_on: Evidence at >=7B, but reported as convergence (loss), with most ablations at 2B and short runs.

findings.claim: The residual is the token+position embedding plus a sum of projections confined to the subspace; the receiver rebuilds the embedding term from token ids.
findings.quote: Therefore, we consider the rank of the residual activations when PE and TE are subtracted
findings.bears_on: The boundary carries k coefficients plus token ids (b_tok), so d_eff*b_a can approach the cost of the tokens themselves.

findings.claim: Generic compressors fail at the same 100x ratio.
findings.quote: Top-k, low-rank (SVD), and quantization fail to converge at 100×
findings.bears_on: 100x requires the architectural change; post-hoc codecs on standard models do not reach it.

title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in transformer-based language models
authors: David Raposo, Sam Ritter, Blake Richards, Timothy Lillicrap, Peter Conway Humphreys, Adam Santoro

findings.claim: Mixture-of-Depths can improve the training objective by up to 1.5% at equal training FLOPs and wall-clock.
findings.quote: one can train an MoD transformer that improves upon vanilla transformers by as much as 1.5% on the final log probability training objective for equivalent training FLOPs (isoFLOP)
findings.bears_on: Token-level conditional depth: m_A slightly above 1.

title: Activations and Gradients Compression for Model-Parallel Training
authors: Mikhail Rudakov, Aleksandr Beznosikov, Yaroslav Kholodov, Alexander Gasnikov

findings.claim: In model-parallel training, boundary activations tolerate 2-4 bit quantization but activation-gradients need at least 6 bits for uncompressed-level accuracy.
findings.quote: Test accuracy comparable to uncompressed scenario is achieved only when gradients are quantized to at least 6 bits, while activations may be quantized to 2 or 4 bits.

quantities.condition: forward boundary activations (2 bits also comparable); ResNet18 on CIFAR-10; compression must stay on at inference
backward boundary activation-gradients, minimum for comparable accuracy; same setup

findings.bears_on: Backward b_a needs more bits than forward, consistent with TAH-Quant; small-scale only.

title: SWARM Parallelism: Training Large Models Can Be Surprisingly Communication-Efficient
authors: Max Ryabinin, Tim Dettmers, Michael Diskin, Alexander Borzunov

findings.claim: Activations and their gradients at pipeline boundaries are sent with dynamic blockwise 8-bit quantization.
findings.quote: Instead, we use dynamic 8-bit quantization with blockwise scaling from (Dettmers et al., 2022). This technique reduces communication by ≈2x and ≈4x for half and full precision, respectively.

quantities.condition: forward activations and backward gradients at pipeline boundaries; training

findings.bears_on: 8-bit boundary activations in training are the established safe choice.

findings.claim: 8-bit compression did not slow convergence, while a 2x linear or maxout bottleneck cost 26-28% more steps.
findings.quote: We can see that 8-bit compression does not degrade the time to 22 perplexity and maintains close to the final perplexity of the baseline. The compression-aware bottleneck and maxout architectures perform equal to each other, but degrade final perplexity slightly and increase time to a perplexity of 22 by 26–28%.

quantities.condition: 8-bit quantization vs 16-bit: no slowdown; WikiText-103 LM, 2 stages
bottleneck c = m/2 costs 26-28% more steps to target perplexity

findings.bears_on: Halving the boundary dimension of a standard model is not free; supports intrinsic_dim near 1 without architecture redesign.

title: ESPACE: Dimensionality Reduction of Activations for Model Compression
authors: Charbel Sakr, Brucek Khailany

findings.claim: Projecting GEMM-input activations onto precomputed principal components gives 50% model compression with small loss after retraining.
findings.quote: Experimentally, we find ESPACE enables 50% compression of GPT3, Llama2, and Nemotron4 models with small accuracy degradation, as low as a 0.18 perplexity increase on GPT3-22B.

quantities.condition: derived from the paper's own example: 50% compression of a square layer means L = K/4; GPT3-22B +0.18 ppl; with retraining

findings.bears_on: A linear projection keeps about a quarter of each matmul input's dimensions at small loss; central anchor for d_eff.

findings.claim: The paper states how 50% compression maps to projection rank.
findings.quote: For instance, if N = K, i.e., WT is square, and L = K/4, then our method yields 50% compression at inference time.
findings.bears_on: Converts the headline into a dimension fraction; each GEMM has its own projection, so the shared residual needs more.

title: Massive Activations in Large Language Models
authors: Mingjie Sun, Xinlei Chen, J. Zico Kolter, Zhuang Liu

findings.claim: A handful of residual entries are up to 100,000x larger than the rest, nearly input-independent, and act as bias terms.
findings.quote: we find their values largely stay constant regardless of the input, and they function as indispensable bias terms in LLMs.

quantities.condition: number of massive activations in LLaMA2-7B whose zeroing collapses the model; setting them to their mean is harmless

findings.bears_on: The outliers that break naive low-bit quantization carry little per-token information, so they can be predicted from committed weights.

findings.claim: Zeroing four massive activations collapses LLaMA2-7B, but setting them to their means is harmless.
findings.quote: For instance, in LLaMA2-7B, setting merely four massive activations (out of millions of activations) to zero would result in catastrophic collapse in model performance. Further, setting them to their mean values does not hurt the model
findings.bears_on: Supports encoding these few entries as constants, which lowers effective b_a.

title: Training LLMs with MXFP4
authors: Albert Tseng, Tao Yu, Youngsuk Park

findings.claim: MXFP4 on every backward-pass GEMM input of the decoder linear layers (including the activation-gradients), made unbiased with stochastic rounding and a random Hadamard transform, matches BF16 validation loss at 1.3B on 210B tokens and at 6.7B on 21B tokens. The forward pass stays BF16.
findings.quote: Pretrain GPT models up to 6.7B and show that our training recipe closes the MXFP4-BF16 gap to <0.1 validation perplexity.

quantities.condition: derived: FP4 E2M1 + one 8-bit scale per 32 (4 + 8/32); backward GEMM inputs (dL/dy, weights, saved activations) with RHT + stochastic rounding; forward BF16; GPT 1.3B / 210B tokens val loss 2.29 vs BF16 2.29, 6.7B / 21B tokens 2.27 vs 2.27 (Table 2); GEMM-input precision, the transmitted tensors stay BF16

findings.bears_on: Backward-pass b_a can be about 4.25 bits at no measurable loss at 1.3B/210B, but only with unbiased rounding, and the forward pass was not quantized.

findings.claim: Without stochastic rounding or the Hadamard transform, MXFP4 in only the backward pass raises GPT 1.3B validation loss from 2.32 to 2.40 on 42B tokens.
findings.quote: As we show in Section 4, directly using MXFP4 in even only the backward pass of decoder linear layers significantly degrades model quality.

quantities.condition: naive round-to-nearest MXFP4 backward, forward BF16; GPT 1.3B / 42B tokens val loss 2.40 vs 2.32 (derived +3.4%); 345M / 33B 2.60 vs 2.49 (Table 2)

findings.bears_on: Negative result: biased 4-bit backward rounding costs about 3% loss, so 4.25 bits backward needs unbiased estimators.

title: The geometry of hidden representations of large transformer models
authors: Lucrezia Valeriani, Diego Doimo, Francesca Cuturello, Alessandro Laio, Alessio Ansuini, Alberto Cazzaniga

findings.claim: The intrinsic dimension of hidden representations rises early, then contracts in middle layers; values stay in the tens.
findings.quote: In the first layers, the data manifold expands, becoming high-dimensional, and then contracts significantly in the intermediate layers.

quantities.condition: upper end of Figure 1 ID axis; ESM-2 up to 3B and iGPT up to 1.4B (protein/image transformers)

findings.bears_on: Representation manifolds are tens of dimensions; supports a very low intrinsic_dim, though for non-language models.

title: Fine-tuning Language Models over Slow Networks using Activation Compression with Guarantees
authors: Jue Wang, Binhang Yuan, Luka Rimanic, Yongjun He, Tri Dao, Beidi Chen, et al.

findings.claim: Compressing the change in each example's activation since its last visit allows 2-4 bit pipeline activations in fine-tuning up to 1.5B, where direct quantization fails.
findings.quote: We show that AQ-SGD can aggressively quantize activations to 2-4 bits without sacrificing convergence performance, where direct quantization of activations fails to converge

quantities.condition: forward, DeBERTa-1.5B fine-tuning (fw2 bw4); GPT2-1.5B used fw3 bw6; delta vs per-example buffer
derived: 16-bit / 2-bit forward

findings.bears_on: Lowest b_a demonstrated for training across a pipeline boundary, but only via delta coding on repeated examples.

findings.claim: Backward gradients were sent at twice the forward bit width.
findings.quote: AQ-SGD (fw2 bw4)

quantities.condition: backward activation-gradient bits with 2-bit forward activations

findings.bears_on: A training boundary carries forward and backward traffic; the backward needs more bits.

findings.claim: The first time an example is seen, its activation is sent uncompressed.
findings.quote: if it is the first time that ξt is sampled, Machine a communicates the full precision activations without any compression
findings.bears_on: In single-epoch pretraining AQ-SGD gives no compression; its low b_a relies on information the receiver already holds.

findings.claim: The per-example buffer is large.
findings.quote: in GPT2-XL training, a simple calculation shows that we need an approximately extra 1TB storage.
findings.bears_on: Delta coding trades boundary bits for stored state, which NCI would count as previously read information.

title: BitNet a4.8: 4-bit Activations for 1-bit LLMs
authors: Hongyu Wang, Shuming Ma, Furu Wei

findings.claim: Trained ternary-weight models use 4-bit inputs to attention and FFN, and sparsified 8-bit intermediate states.
findings.quote: Specifically, we utilize 4-bit activations for inputs to the attention and feed-forward network layers, while sparsifying intermediate states followed with 8-bit quantization.

quantities.condition: INT4/FP4 inputs to attention/FFN; quantization-aware training (STE), 7B, 100B tokens; backward in high precision
supports 3-bit KV cache

findings.bears_on: Models trained for low-bit activations reach 4 bits at 7B; intermediate (FFN-down/attention-output) states still need 8 bits.
findings.audit: 2026-10-17 sample audit: quote yes, claim yes, quantities yes

findings.claim: At 7B, BitNet a4.8 matches BitNet b1.58 with almost no loss.
findings.quote: For 7B models, BitNet b1.58 matches LLaMA LLM in terms of both language model perplexity and average accuracy on the end tasks. Furthermore, BitNet a4.8 achieves performance comparable to BitNet b1.58, with almost no loss in average accuracy.
findings.bears_on: Supports b_a=4 at retained quality when the model is trained for it.

title: COAT: Compressing Optimizer States and Activation for Memory-Efficient FP8 Training
authors: Haocheng Xi, Han Cai, Ligeng Zhu, Yao Lu, Kurt Keutzer, Jianfei Chen, et al.

findings.claim: Activations saved for the backward pass can be stored in FP8 with nearly lossless pretraining (OLMo-7B, 250B tokens).

quantities.condition: FP8 stored activations (mixed per-tensor/per-group); OLMo-7B pretraining 250B tokens, Llama-2-7B fine-tuning

findings.bears_on: 8-bit activations survive training including the backward pass; consistent with the high end of b_a.

title: Jetfire: Efficient and Accurate Transformer Pretraining with INT8 Data Flow and Per-Block Quantization
authors: Haocheng Xi, Yuxiang Chen, Kang Zhao, Kai Jun Teh, Jianfei Chen, Jun Zhu

findings.claim: INT8 data flow between operators with per-block quantization matches FP16 pretraining for GPT-2 up to 774M.
findings.quote: Extensive experiments demonstrate that our INT8 FQT method achieves comparable accuracy to the FP16 training baseline and outperforms the existing INT8 training works for transformers.

quantities.condition: INT8 activations/gradients in data flow; GPT2-base/medium/large (124M-774M) pretraining

findings.bears_on: Small-scale support that 8-bit activations moved between operators survive training.

title: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
authors: Guangxuan Xiao, Ji Lin, Mickael Seznec, Hao Wu, Julien Demouth, Song Han

findings.claim: Migrating activation outliers into weights allows W8A8 for all matmuls of LLMs up to 530B with negligible accuracy loss.
findings.quote: SmoothQuant enables an INT8 quantization of both weights and activations for all the matrix multiplications in LLMs, including OPT, BLOOM, GLM, MT-NLG, Llama-1/2, Falcon, Mistral, and Mixtral models.

quantities.condition: W8A8 post-training quantization, inference only; up to MT-NLG 530B; negligible loss

findings.bears_on: Confirms 8-bit activations are routine in inference at the largest scales; does not lower b_a below 8.

title: Echo: Error-Compensated 4-Bit Tensor-Parallel Communication for LLM Training and Inference
authors: Xingyu Xie, Xiaoyong Xie, Zhouchen Lin, Kim-Chuan Toh

findings.claim: A 4-bit tensor-parallel all-reduce with error feedback and high-precision summation, used at every forward and backward TP site, ends 10B-token Qwen3-0.6B pretraining 0.9% above 16-bit loss, with a slightly higher learning rate.
findings.quote: Over the last 100 steps (tail-100), the 4-bit loss averages 3.225 and the 16-bit loss 3.197, a gap of 0.027 computed before rounding, less than 0.9% of the 16-bit loss.

findings.bears_on: The only published 4-bit TP partial-sum pretraining: 4.25 bits at a 0.9% loss, small model, with error-feedback state at each site.

findings.claim: At inference the compensated 4-bit TP all-reduce raises Llama-3-8B perplexity by 0.29; uncompensated it raises it by 0.66, and 8 bits leaves it unchanged.
findings.quote: 4-bit path raises perplexity by 0.29 on Llama-3-8B (6.07 to 6.36) and by 0.10 on Qwen3-8B (9.70 to 9.80), and the 8-bit path leaves it unchanged.

quantities.condition: TP all-reduce partial sums at inference, with compensator; Llama-3-8B WikiText ppl 6.07 -> 6.36; without compensation 6.73; Qwen3-8B 9.70 -> 9.80 (10.45 uncompensated)

findings.bears_on: Error feedback halves the 4-bit partial-sum penalty; 8-bit partial sums are lossless at 8B inference.

title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models
authors: Zhenyu Zhang, Ying Sheng, Tianyi Zhou, Tianlong Chen, Lianmin Zheng, Ruisi Cai, et al.

findings.claim: Keeping only recent and heavy-hitter tokens (20% of the KV) preserves accuracy, cutting KV memory up to 5x.
findings.quote: can reduce the memory footprint of $\kv\cache$ by up to $5\times$ without accuracy degradation on a wide range of model architectures (OPT, LLaMA, GPT-NeoX), sizes (from 6.7B to 175B)

authors: Tianyi Zhang, Jonah Yi, Zhaozhuo Xu, Anshumali Shrivastava

findings.claim: KV channels are strongly inter-dependent, so jointly coding channels beats per-channel quantization.
findings.quote: the joint entropy of multiple channels grows at a slower rate than the sum of their marginal entropies
findings.bears_on: Entropy coding across channels can push b_a.kv (and likely b_a) below per-entry quantization widths.

findings.claim: At 2 bits per entry coupled quantization costs +0.29 perplexity on LLaMA-7B; at 1 bit it costs +2.41.

LLaMA-7b ppl 5.68 -> 8.09 (CQ-8c8b); 1.25 bits gives 6.78

title: Hyper-Connections
authors: Defa Zhu, Hongzhi Huang, Zihao Huang, Yutao Zeng, Yunyao Mao, Banggu Wu et al.

findings.claim: Hyper-connections make OLMoE-1B-7B converge 1.8x faster than residual connections, with the gain kept at 500B tokens.

findings.bears_on: m_A about 1.8 for an MoE at 1B active parameters.

findings.claim: The hidden state is replicated n times into an n x d hyper hidden matrix (n is the expansion rate).

quantities.condition: expansion rate n of the OLMoE-1B-7B-DHC result

title: BiSup: Bidirectional Quantization Error Suppression for Large Language Models
authors: Minghui Zou, Ronghui Guo, Sai Zhang, Xiaowang Zhang, Zhiyong Feng

findings.claim: At W3A3 (group 128) even the best method leaves large losses, and plain QuaRot collapses on Llama-3-8B.
findings.quote: the average WikiText2 perplexity decreases from 13.26 to 9.41 for Atom and from 14.33 to 7.85 for QuaRot under the W3A3-g128 configuration

quantities.condition: W3A3-g128 PTQ+PEFT; Llama-1/2/3 7B-30B average WikiText-2 ppl 7.85 (BiSup) vs FP16 ~5.2; inference

findings.bears_on: 3-bit activations are not yet at retained quality in inference; argues against b_a below ~4 without training.

findings.claim: On Llama-3-8B, W3A3-g128 drops average zero-shot accuracy from 74.49 to 44.91 (QuaRot) or 60.53 (QuaRot+BiSup).

quantities.condition: Llama-3-8B W3A3-g128: avg acc 74.49 (FP16) -> 60.53 best; weights also 3-bit

findings.bears_on: Quantifies the quality cost of 3-bit activations (with 3-bit weights) at 8B: large.
